paragraphs.en: Dorothy awoke suddenly from a jarring shock, which made her gasp and wonder what had happened. Toto's cold nose nuzzled her face, adding to her confusion. She sat up, noticing the house wasn't moving, and the bright sunlight flooded the room.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西猛然从一阵刺耳的惊吓中醒来，不由得倒抽了一口冷气，疑惑发生了什么。托托冰冷的小鼻子蹭了蹭她的脸，更让她感到困惑。她坐起身来，发现房子并没有移动，明亮的日光倾泻进房间。

paragraphs.en: Amazed by the sight before her, Dorothy sprang out of bed with Toto following. The cyclone had gently set the house in a land of breathtaking beauty. Green meadows surrounded them, dotted with stately trees bearing lush fruits.
paragraphs.zh: 惊异于眼前景象，多萝西带着托托跳下床。龙卷风轻柔地将房子安置在一片令人心旷神怡的土地上。四周是翠绿的草地，点缀着高大的树木，树上挂满了丰饶的果实。

paragraphs.en: Flowers of every color bloomed around, and birds sang melodiously from the branches.
paragraphs.zh: 五彩斑斓的花朵在四周绽放，枝头上的鸟儿婉转歌唱。

paragraphs.en: A small brook flowed nearby, its clear waters sparkling as it murmured soothingly. This was a stark contrast to Dorothy's usual life on the dry prairies.
paragraphs.zh: 一条清澈的小溪潺潺流过附近，水珠在轻声细语中闪烁着光芒。这与多萝西平时在干旱平原上的生活形成了鲜明的对比。

paragraphs.en: As she gazed at the strange sights, a group approached her. These people were neither tall nor short; they seemed about Dorothy’s height, who was well-grown for her age. Three men and one woman, all dressed oddly, met her gaze.
paragraphs.zh: 当她注视着这些奇异的景象时，一群人朝她走来。这些人既不高大也不矮小，看起来和多萝西差不多高，而多萝西在她的年龄里算是个子挺高的。三个男人和一个女人，全都穿着奇装异服，目光与她相遇。

paragraphs.en: Their round hats with tinkling bells around the brims added to their peculiar appearance.
paragraphs.zh: 他们戴着圆顶帽，帽边系着叮当作响的铃铛，更增添了他们那独特的外观。

paragraphs.en: The men wore blue hats and boots, while the little woman had a white hat and gown adorned with twinkling stars. Dorothy thought the men looked about as old as Uncle Henry, given their beards, but the woman appeared much older, her face lined and hair nearly white.
paragraphs.zh: 这些男人戴着蓝色的帽子和靴子，而那个矮小的女人则戴着一顶白色帽子，并穿着绣有闪烁星星的长裙。多萝西见他们都有胡子，便觉得这些男人大概和亨利叔叔年纪相仿，但那女人看起来要老得多，脸上布满了皱纹，头发几乎全白了。

paragraphs.en: When the people approached Dorothy's house, they hesitated, whispering among themselves. The old woman stepped forward, bowed, and spoke sweetly:
paragraphs.zh: 当人们走近多萝西的房子时，他们犹豫不决，低声议论着。老妇人走上前去，躬身施礼，语气温柔地说道：

paragraphs.en: "You are welcome, noble Sorceress, to our land of the Munchkins. We thank you for defeating the Wicked Witch of the East."
paragraphs.zh: “欢迎你，高贵的女巫，来到我们的 munchkinland。感谢你击败了东方恶witch。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy was surprised by these words. She had never killed anything in her life, just a girl carried by a cyclone.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西听到这话感到惊讶。她从未亲手害死过任何东西，只是被龙卷风带过来的一个小女孩而已。

paragraphs.en: The old woman expected Dorothy's response and said hesitantly, "You must have made a mistake. I haven't killed anyone."
paragraphs.zh: 老妇人预料到多萝西会这样回答，犹豫着说：“你一定是搞错了。我没杀过任何人。”

paragraphs.en: "Your house did," replied the old woman with a laugh, pointing to the corner of the house. "See those feet sticking out from under a block of wood?"
paragraphs.zh: “你的房子就是这样的，”老妇人笑着回答，指着房子的一个角落，“你看，那些脚不是露在木块下面吗？”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy gasped as she saw two silver-shod feet. The house had fallen on someone.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西惊呼一声，只见两双银鞋的脚露了出来。房子压在了某个人身上。

paragraphs.en: "Oh, dear! What shall we do?" cried Dorothy in dismay.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，天哪！我们该怎么办呢？”多萝西惊慌失措地喊道。

paragraphs.en: "There's nothing we can do," said the old woman calmly.
paragraphs.zh: “我们无能为力了，”那位老妇人冷静地说。

paragraphs.en: "Who was she?" asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: “她是谁？”多萝西问道。

paragraphs.en: "She was the Wicked Witch of the East," answered the old woman. "She enslaved our people for years. Now they are free and grateful to you."
paragraphs.zh: “她是东方的恶巫,”老妇人回答道,“她曾多年奴役我们的子民。现在他们自由了，感激你所做的一切。”

paragraphs.en: "Who are the Munchkins?" Dorothy inquired further.
paragraphs.zh: “ munchkins 是谁？”多萝西继续问道。

paragraphs.en: "They live in this eastern land where the witch ruled."
paragraphs.zh: 它们生活在女巫统治的东方土地上。

paragraphs.en: "Are you a Munchkin?" Dorothy asked.
paragraphs.zh: “你是 munchkin 吗？”多萝西问道。

paragraphs.en: "No, but I am their friend," replied the old woman. "I came from the North when they sent a swift messenger after learning of the Witch's death."
paragraphs.zh: “不是的，但我却是他们的朋友。”老妇人回答道，“我在巫婆去世后不久便从北方赶来，他们派了一个快速使者通知了我。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, gracious!" exclaimed Dorothy. "Are you a real witch?"
paragraphs.zh: “哦，天哪！”多萝西脱口而出，“你真是一个巫婆吗？”

paragraphs.en: The little woman replied, "Yes, indeed, but I am a good witch, loved by the people. If I were as powerful as the Wicked Witch who ruled here, I would have freed them myself."
paragraphs.zh: 小妇人回答说：“是的，确实如此，但我是一个受人们爱戴的好巫婆。如果我像统治这里的恶毒巫婆那样强大，早就把他们解放了。”

paragraphs.en: "Didn't you know all witches are wicked?" asked the girl, half frightened.
paragraphs.zh: “你不知道所有的巫婆都是邪恶的吗？”那个女孩半是害怕地问道。

paragraphs.en: "No, that's a mistake," said the witch. "There were only four witches in Oz—two good ones in the North and South, and two wicked ones in the East and West. Now there’s just one Wicked Witch left."
paragraphs.zh: “不，那是个误会，”女巫说道，“奥兹国只有四个女巫——北方和南方各有一个好女巫，东方和西方各有一个恶女巫。现在只剩下最后一个恶女巫了。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy remembered Aunt Em saying all witches were dead long ago. The witch asked, "Who is Aunt Em?"
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西想起艾姆姨妈曾说过所有的巫婆早就不在了。女巫问道：“艾姆姨妈是谁？”

paragraphs.en: "She lives in Kansas," Dorothy explained.
paragraphs.zh: “她住在堪萨斯州，”多萝西解释道。

paragraphs.en: The witch thought for a moment, then said, "I've never heard of Kansas. But tell me—is it civilized?"
paragraphs.zh: 巫婆想了想，然后说道：“我可没听说过堪萨斯州。不过告诉我——那边的社会还算文明吗？”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, it is," replied Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，就是它。”多丽丝回答道。

paragraphs.en: "That explains it," the witch continued. "In civilized lands, there are no witches or wizards. Oz has never been civilized, so we still have them."
paragraphs.zh: “这就解释了原因，”女巫继续说道，“在文明之地，没有巫师和魔法师和巫婆。奥兹从未成为文明之地，所以我们这里还有。”

paragraphs.en: "Who are the wizards?" asked Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: “那些巫师都是谁？”多萝西问道。

paragraphs.en: "The Great Wizard is Oz himself," whispered the witch. "He's more powerful than all of us combined and lives in the City of Emeralds."
paragraphs.zh: “大巫师就是奥兹本人，”女巫低语道，“他的力量远超我们所有人之和，他住在翡翠城。”

paragraphs.en: Just then, the Munchkins shouted, pointing to where the Wicked Witch had been lying. The witch looked and laughed as she saw that the dead Witch’s feet were gone, leaving only silver shoes behind.
paragraphs.zh: 就在这时，小人国居民们喊叫着，指着巫婆倒下的地方。只见巫婆看了看，露出了笑容，因为那死去的巫婆的双脚已经消失不见，只剩下一对银鞋留在原地。

paragraphs.en: The Witch of the North handed Dorothy her silver shoes, explaining that they were hers to keep. A Munchkin mentioned a charm connected to them but never knew its specifics.
paragraphs.zh: 北方女巫将银色舞鞋递给多萝西，解释说这些鞋子归她所有，可以留着。一个 munchkin 提到与鞋子有关的一个咒语，但从未具体了解过详情。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy brought the shoes inside and placed them on the table. She then returned to the group and expressed her desire to return home to her aunt and uncle. The Munchkins and Witch exchanged glances, then shook their heads.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西把鞋子带进屋，放在桌子上。然后她回到众人中间，表达了想回家的愿望，希望回到她的姨妈和叔叔那里去。 munchkins 和巫婆交换了一下眼神，随后都摇了摇头。

paragraphs.en: One Munchkin spoke of a vast desert at the eastern border, impassable for anyone. Another mentioned the southern Quadlings' land, while a third warned about the western Winkies ruled by the Wicked Witch of the West.
paragraphs.zh: 一位芒奇金提到东部边境有一片广阔的沙漠，对任何人来说都无法穿越。另一位提到了南部夸地利亚人的土地，而第三位则警告大家西部由西方恶女巫统治的温基人地区充满了危险。

paragraphs.en: The old lady, Dorothy's host, said that the northern desert surrounded their land and suggested Dorothy stay with them. This news made Dorothy cry, feeling lonely among strangers.
paragraphs.zh: 老妇人，多萝西的东道主，说他们这片土地被北方的沙漠环绕，并建议多萝西留下来。这个消息让多萝西不禁泪眼婆娑，在陌生人的中间感到格外孤独。

paragraphs.en: Seeing her distress, the kind-hearted Munchkins offered handkerchiefs to wipe away her tears. The old woman took off her cap, balanced it on her nose, and counted "One, two, three." Instantly, the cap transformed into a slate with large white chalk marks: "LET DOROTHY GO TO THE CITY OF EMERALDS."
paragraphs.zh: 见她如此伤心，善良的芒奇金人递给她手帕让她擦眼泪。老妇人摘下帽子，顶在鼻尖上，数道：“一、二、三。”转瞬间，帽子变成了一个大大的石板，上面用白粉写着：“让多萝西去翡翠城。”

paragraphs.en: The old lady removed the slate, read the message aloud, then asked Dorothy if her name was indeed Dorothy. The child confirmed it, and the woman said that perhaps Oz would help her.
paragraphs.zh: 老妇人收起石板，高声念完信上的内容，然后问多丽丝是否真的叫多丽丝。孩子点了点头，老妇人说或许奥兹能帮她一把。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy inquired about the location of this city, which the old lady explained was exactly at the center of their land, ruled by the Great Wizard Oz.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西询问这座城市的地理位置，老妇人解释说这座城市正好位于他们的土地正中心，并由伟大的奥兹巫师统治。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy asked anxiously, "Is he a good man?" The old Witch replied, "He is a good Wizard. I cannot say if he's a man; I've never seen him."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西焦虑地问道：“他是个好人吗？”老巫婆回答说：“他是个好巫师。我不能说他是个人；我从未见过他。”

paragraphs.en: "How can I get there?" Dorothy inquired. "You must walk," the Witch explained.
paragraphs.zh: “我怎么才能到那里去？”多萝西问道。“你必须步行。”女巫解释道。

paragraphs.en: "It’s a long journey through a country that is sometimes pleasant and sometimes dark and terrible. But I will use all my magic to keep you safe."
paragraphs.zh: “这段旅程穿越的是一片时而宁静宜人、时而阴暗恐怖的土地。但我会动用所有的魔法来保护你。”

paragraphs.en: "Will you go with me?" Dorothy pleaded, seeing the old woman as her only friend.
paragraphs.zh: “你愿意和我一起去吗？”多萝西恳求道，只见那位老妇人是她唯一的挚友。

paragraphs.en: "No, I cannot do that," she replied. "But I'll give you my kiss; no one will dare harm a person kissed by the Witch of the North."
paragraphs.zh: “不，我不能那样做，”她回答道，“但我可以吻你；没有人敢对北国女巫吻过的人下手。”

paragraphs.en: She approached and gently kissed Dorothy on the forehead, leaving a round, shining mark. The girl noticed it soon after.
paragraphs.zh: 她走近后轻吻了多丽丝的前额，留下了一个圆润、闪耀的印记。女孩很快注意到了这一点。

paragraphs.en: "The road to the City of Emeralds is paved with yellow brick," said the Witch. "You cannot miss it. When you get there, do not be afraid of Oz; tell your story and ask for help."
paragraphs.zh: “通向翡翠城的道路铺满了黄色砖块，”女巫说道，“你不会走错的。到了那里，不要害怕奥兹；讲出你的故事并请求帮助。”

paragraphs.en: The three Munchkins bowed low and wished her a pleasant journey before walking away through the trees. Dorothy noticed Toto barking loudly after the Witch disappeared with a whirl.
paragraphs.zh: 三个小人弯下腰来向她祝好，并且在女巫消失时带着一阵旋风穿过树林走开了。朵丽丝注意到托蒂在女巫消失后大声地叫了起来。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy was not surprised by the Witch's disappearance, knowing she could vanish in that manner.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西并不惊讶女巫消失了，因为她知道女巫可以以这种方式凭空消失。
